title: The Heterogeneous Bank Lending Channel of Monetary Policy
coauthors: Jorge Abad, Saki Bigio, Salomon Garcia-Villegas, Joël Marbet
series: NBER WP 35239; CEPR DP 21519; Banco de España WP 2620
summary: Quantitative model of heterogeneous banks: differences in interest-rate risk exposure (fixed- vs variable-rate lending) matter for monetary transmission only when bank solvency concerns bind.
topic: Monetary policy, banking and macro-finance

title: Monetary Policy with Supply Regimes
summary: Globally optimal monetary policy in a New Keynesian model with regimes of persistently higher costs (tariffs, wars, fragmentation): commitment tolerates temporary inflation, discretion creates an inflationary bias.
topic: Monetary policy, banking and macro-finance

title: Firm Heterogeneity, Capital Misallocation and Optimal Monetary Policy
series: CEPR DP 18695; ECB WP 2890; BIS WP 1148
summary: Capital misallocation across heterogeneous firms with financial frictions creates a new expansion motive for monetary policy, but approximate price stability remains optimal except after cost-push shocks.
topic: Monetary policy, banking and macro-finance

title: Decomposing Optimal Debt Maturity
summary: A value-gap rule decomposes optimal sovereign debt maturity into hedging, self-insurance, credit-risk and dilution forces; hedging dominates and the model recommends longer maturities.
topic: Monetary policy, banking and macro-finance

title: Asset Pricing with Heterogeneous Agents under Limited Information
summary: Two-way interaction between wealth inequality and asset prices in a heterogeneous-agent model with aggregate risk, solved with neural networks, generating endogenous time-varying risk premia.
topic: Monetary policy, banking and macro-finance

title: Planning against Disasters in Dynamic Production Networks
summary: In nonlinear multisector production networks the planner over-invests in upstream sectors to mitigate cascading disasters, implying a much larger welfare cost of business cycles (solved with deep learning).
topic: Monetary policy, banking and macro-finance

title: The Redistributive Effects of Sectoral Shocks
summary: Heterogeneous-agent input-output model showing how sectoral shocks propagate through production networks and redistribute income and wealth.
topic: Monetary policy, banking and macro-finance

title: Green Asset Pricing
summary: Empirically grounding the stochastic discount factor raises the optimal carbon price by 32% and makes it far more procyclical, reducing risk premia and precautionary saving.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

title: Weitzman Meets Taylor: EU Allowance Price Drivers and Carbon Cap Rules
summary: Estimated cap-and-trade DSGE on EU ETS data: abatement-cost shocks drive permit-price volatility; a Taylor-rule-like carbon cap rule cuts volatility from over 40% to under 4%.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

title: Beneath the Trees: The Influence of Natural Capital on Shadow Price Dynamics in a Macroeconomic Model with Uncertainty
coauthors: Aditya Mori, Josselin Roman, Romano Tarsia
summary: DSGE with renewable and non-renewable natural capital degraded by temperature: natural capital raises the social cost of carbon by about 10% relative to DICE, much more under shocks.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

title: The Distributional Costs of Net-Zero: A Heterogeneous Agent Perspective
summary: Heterogeneous-agent model of the US 2050 net-zero target: long-run welfare gain but a 6-10% rise in financially constrained households; carbon-revenue redistribution smooths the transition.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

title: Unveiling the Green Equity Premium: A Macro-Financial Outlook
coauthors: Rhys Bidder, Simone Maso, Aditya Mori, Josselin Roman
summary: New greenness classification based on EU ETS exposure: greener Euro-area assets earn a positive premium when carbon prices are low that shrinks as policy commitment rises; climate-sentiment shocks drive returns.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

title: Policy Interactions and the Transition to Clean Technology
summary: Two-sector green/brown DSGE with financial frictions: macroprudential climate risk-weights and green-tilted QE can close the welfare wedge and risk-premium distortion created by the EU ETS.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

title: Carbon Pricing with Regressive Co-benefits: Evidence from British Columbia's Carbon Tax
summary: BC's 2008 carbon tax cut PM2.5 emissions by 5-11% with large monetised co-benefits, but widened pollution-exposure disparities across income and racial groups.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

title: More than just carbon: the socioeconomic co-benefits of large-scale tree planting
summary: Philippines' National Greening Program (2011-2018): large-scale tree planting reduced local poverty by about 6 pp, shifted labour out of agriculture and sequestered 71-303 MtCO2.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

faculty: Ainara González de San Román; Patricia Gabaldón; Liliana Gelabert
title: Board Gender Diversity and Environmental Performance: Association or Pre-existing Firm Dynamics?
series: SSRN (earlier title: Unveiling the Myth: A Causal Reassessment of Gender Diversity's Impact on Corporate Environmental Performance)
status: Under review, Journal of Corporate Finance
summary: S&P 500 panel 2010-2020: the positive association between women on boards and environmental performance disappears under staggered DiD because firms go green before appointing women directors.
topic: Climate economics, carbon pricing and the green transition

title: Freed from the Boys: How Single-Sex Schooling Shapes Girls' Effort and Performance in High-Stakes Exams
coauthors: Caterina Calsamiglia, Yarine Fawaz, Junhee Lee
summary: Lottery-based school assignment: girls placed in single-sex schools exert more effort and outperform boys in high-stakes math exams, at the cost of higher stress and worse mental health.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: Maternity Benefits, Consumption and Labor Supply: Estimating Causal Effects with Bank Transaction Data
coauthors: Libertad González, Alberto Graziano, Josep Mestres
summary: Regression discontinuity with bank transaction data: a large cash transfer to new mothers in Madrid raised consumption of liquidity-constrained women without reducing their labor earnings.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: Private Schooling and Fertility Decline in India
status: Reject and resubmit, Journal of Population Economics
summary: The expansion of fee-based private schooling raised the cost of child quality and, interacting with son preference, generated gender-differentiated fertility stopping that contributed to India's fertility decline.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: Childhood Exposure to Joint Custody Reforms and Adult Family Formation
summary: Staggered US joint-custody reforms and 13 million ACS observations: childhood exposure reduces adult fertility by 7 percent for both women and men, mainly via lower parenthood and couple formation.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: The 'Superwoman Effect' of Female Representation in Animated Series on Gender Roles and Educational Achievements
summary: TV-signal coverage in early-2000s Ukraine: girls exposed to female-led superhero cartoons attain more education, choose STEM more often and hold less traditional gender stereotypes.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: Just the Flu? The Labor Market Spillovers of Influenza Vaccination
summary: Difference-in-differences using variation in US flu-vaccine quality and local vaccination rates: influenza vaccination raises employment and wages, with productivity, demand and sectoral spillover channels.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow: How Response Times Can Predict Cognitive Decline and (Bad) Financial Decision-Making at Older Ages
series: Working paper (presented at NBER Summer Institute 2025)
summary: Interview response times in SHARE predict subsequent cognitive decline, health deterioration and wealth losses among older Europeans, especially for those unaware of their own decline.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: Income, Employment and Health Risks of Older Workers
summary: Using the US HRS, models older workers' transitions to bridge jobs and retirement, separating health, productivity, mismatch and job-destruction risks, and quantifies the welfare cost of mismatch risk.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: Estimating Choice Models with Piecewise Smooth Objective Functions: Application to Joint Retirement
summary: Method for estimating choice models with piecewise smooth objective functions (stochastic EM), applied to joint retirement of European couples; finds complementarity between spouses in exiting the labor force.
topic: Fertility, Ageing, Demographic Transition and Health

title: From Pilot to Policy: Experimental Evidence from Scaling Online Tutoring
coauthors: María Calle, Lucas Gortazar, María Hernández-de-Benito, Claudia Hupkau, Teresa Molina-Millán
summary: RCT of an online math tutoring programme scaled up by regional education authorities in Spain: effects are about one-third of the pilot's, quantifying the voltage drop when scaling evidence-based interventions.
topic: Education, technology and public policy

title: Digital Infrastructure and Work Organization: Evidence from Spain's FTTH Rollout
summary: Causal effects of fiber-to-the-home broadband expansion in Spain, exploiting its staggered provincial rollout 2012-2023, on how work is organized and how households allocate time.
topic: Education, technology and public policy

title: A Collective Review on Some Potential Negative Impacts of Smartphone and Social Media Use on Adolescent Mental Health: Results from a Delphi Process
coauthors: Valerio Capraro, Laura Globig, Zachary Rausch, Steve Rathje and 120+ others
summary: Delphi consensus among 120+ researchers from 11 disciplines on adolescent mental-health trends, causal links to smartphone and social media use, and policy recommendations.
topic: Education, technology and public policy

title: Does Performance Evidence Motivate? A Field Experiment in Guinea-Bissau's Health Sector
series: Working paper (Weiss Family Distinguished Paper, NEUDC 2023)
summary: RCT with Guinea-Bissau's Ministry of Health: giving frontline health workers credible evidence of their programme's impact raised time in direct patient care by 39%.
topic: Development economics

title: For Honor or for Profit? An Experiment on Recruiting Traditional Health Practitioners for Formal Healthcare in Guinea-Bissau
coauthors: Brais Álvarez-Pereira, Teresa Molina-Millán, Pedro C. Vicente
summary: Randomised honor vs. profit recruitment messages for training traditional health practitioners as formal health agents; the profit message raises interest, especially among less religious practitioners.
topic: Development economics
